description: Team Urban Alchemists- BUET undergrads in urban planning, GIS, and data science. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we built PRAAN: a ward-level early-warning system linking GRACE satellite data to climate migration pressure on Dhaka. Looking to add skills in data visualization, web development, and storytelling for our final presentation.
summary:
PRAAN is a trend detective for Bangladesh's water. Using NASA GRACE and GRACE-FO, we measured dry-season water storage from 2002 to 2024 in three regions of Bangladesh with one extraction and one trend test. The Barind Tract in the northwest is falling by 1.04 cm a year over 2002–2017 (Mann-Kendall p = 0.0046), and the decline holds over the full record. Over the same districts MODIS vegetation is rising and CHIRPS rainfall shows no significant trend: the land is getting greener while the water under it runs down, which points to irrigation pumping, not drought.

Anyone can repeat the investigation. The site's Trend Detective lets a user pick one of seven variables (from GRACE, GLDAS, GPM, MODIS and CHIRPS), a region, a season and a range of years. It draws the record, runs Sen's slope and the Mann-Kendall test in the browser, and explains the result in plain language.

We then follow the trend to where its consequences may land: we rank 75 Dhaka wards by the strain rural arrivals could put on them and flag 11 as high concern. A trend visible from space gives planners years of lead time. Every figure is reproducible from our public repository.

Code and data: https://github.com/fmad121581-hub/PRAAN
details:
WHAT IT DOES

The challenge asks what is changing, where, by how much, and whether the change is significant. PRAAN answers all four for water storage over Bangladesh, and gives anyone a tool to ask the same questions of other Earth-system variables.

The Trend Detective answers the same four questions for any variable, region, season and period a user picks: seven variables from GRACE and GRACE-FO, GPM, MODIS, GLDAS and CHIRPS, extracted as monthly means over five regions (script 23) and embedded in the page. The statistics run in the browser from one source file that a test (script 24) checks against our Python pipeline and scipy. Plain-language definitions sit beside every variable and statistical term, and four worked cases guide a first-time user, including one where the answer is "no significant trend". Any view can be shared as a link, and the data behind it downloaded as CSV.

WHAT WE FOUND

What and where. Dry-season (January to May) water-storage anomaly from the JPL GRACE/GRACE-FO mascon product, extracted identically over the Barind Tract, the coastal south and the haor basin. A fourth region around Dhaka returned the same series as the haor basin (correlation 1.000), so we report three independent regions, which is what GRACE's resolution supports.

How much and how significant. Sen's slope and the Mann-Kendall test, with a Hamed-Rao check for serial correlation that is only ever allowed to make a p-value larger. Barind: −1.04 cm/yr, p = 0.0046 (2002–2017) and −0.56 cm/yr, p = 0.0077 (2002–2024). Coastal south: −0.63 cm/yr, p = 0.017 (2002–2017), not significant over 2002–2024 (p = 0.54). Haor basin: not significant in either window. GRACE images are placed by their midpoint date and averaged on the product's native grid (CORRECTIONS.md section 12).

Why. MODIS NDVI over the same districts and season rises significantly, and CHIRPS rainfall shows no significant trend over 39 years. Together these point to irrigation extraction, consistent with Bangladesh Water Development Board tube-well records (Aziz et al. 2015). GRACE measures total water storage, not groundwater alone, so we subtract the soil moisture, snow and canopy water in NASA's GLDAS-2.1 Noah model (the water-balance method of Rodell et al. 2009). The Barind's dry-season remainder still falls: −0.65 cm/yr over 2002–2017 (p = 0.017) and −0.42 cm/yr over 2002–2024 (p = 0.047), about two-thirds of the full decline. That remainder still includes surface water, and GLDAS does not model irrigation, so we call it a groundwater estimate, not a measurement.

So what. Using BBS census data, a migration scenario and an Absorption Stress Index built from WorldPop density, JRC built-up surface, JRC flood history and household crowding, we rank 75 Dhaka wards. 11 are high concern. We tested whether the stress index predicts where people actually moved; it does not, and the site says so.

HOW IT WORKS

Google Earth Engine extracts each dataset to CSV files kept in the repository. Python scripts compute the statistics, and one build script embeds the data in a single HTML page. The site needs no installation or sign-in, runs on a phone, and works offline once loaded.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

PRAAN is built for Dhaka's two city corporations, urban planners and the NGOs that work with low-income arrivals. A trend that is visible from space years before it shows up in a city gives planners lead time: the ward list says where services, drainage and housing pressure are most likely to build first. The site works in a browser with no installation, on a phone, and offline, and the key results link to the CSVs behind them. We want the method to be reused for other Bangladeshi cities, and the code is open for that.

WHAT IS CREATIVE

We treat the trend as a case to investigate, not a chart to show. The same test is run in three regions, so the places with no significant trend are reported beside the one that has it. Three independent satellite records (gravity, vegetation, rainfall) are combined to argue cause. And the trend is followed from an aquifer to the city wards where its consequences may land.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

GRACE resolves about 300 km, so we report three independent regions and no district detail. The groundwater figure is an estimate, not a measurement. The migration numbers are scenarios, not forecasts. Every error we found in our own work, and its fix, is logged publicly in CORRECTIONS.md.

TOOLS

Google Earth Engine for data extraction; Python (NumPy, pandas, SciPy, statsmodels, GeoPandas, scikit-learn, Matplotlib, seaborn) for analysis; a single-file HTML site with Leaflet 1.9.4 and the Archivo typeface, hosted on Netlify; Git and GitHub.

USE OF AI

PRAAN contains no AI and calls no AI service; no number, chart or image is AI-generated. The code is AI-assisted: working from our instructions, Claude (Anthropic) helped write and debug the analysis scripts and the website code, review our statistical methods and edit documentation, and Perplexity helped find literature and data sources. The team chose the problem, data and methods, ran and checked every script, and decided what to claim. Full record: https://github.com/fmad121581-hub/PRAAN/blob/master/docs/AI_USE.md
